newsitem.title: USA: Lott vows to work with Clinton on budget, taxes.
newsitem.headline: Lott vows to work with Clinton on budget, taxes.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott, R-Miss, vowed Tuesday to work with President Clinton on a number of issues including balancing the federal budget, regulatory reform and tax relief.

"Clearly the people voted in a way that indicates they want us to work together ...," Lott said in an interview with CBS News after television networks projected that Republicans would keep control of both the House and Senate while President Clinton served his second term.

"Bill Clinton said he was for less government and less taxes," Lott said. "He talked like a Republican, and if he means that sincerely, we can work together on continuing the work to reduce the deficit and balance the federal budget."

"I think we can come to agreement on some taxes that would be good for the economy and help with economic growth...and make the tax code fairer," he added. "Hopefully we can work together on some regulatory relief and some things like juvenile justice and drug problems."

Congress will also likely hold hearings on the finance issues raised during the campaign and reports of abuses and possible corruption, Lott said, adding that "the emphasis will be on the people's agenda."

Separately, Senate Banking Committee Chairman Alfonse D'Amato, R-N.Y., told a crowd at the Willard Hotel that he favored reducing taxes for working middle-class families, especially those with children, and a cut in the capital gains tax.
"A capital gains tax cut will help the economy," D'Amato said. "I think the economy has not been as robust as it should be."
